title: I Recorded the Food-Truck Propane the Vendor Called a Patio Heater

parts.text: I lived above the food-truck pad and at 10:41 p.m. truck 12 hissed like a small engine. The vendor had told the city it was a patio heater. The pad card on every stall said: PROPANE OFF AT 10. HEATERS ARE ELECTRIC. I was thirty-three, upstairs tenant, holding a video where the tank collar still showed. Vendor Paz said, "That's a quiet heater." I pointed at the card. He cracked the valve. "Heaters have BTUs." I photographed the card, the collar, and a reading of 71 dB. Then I sent a 20-second clip to the pad office. At 10:48 the office asked why truck 12 was on a propane-after-ten ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The pad office can see a tank collar and 71 dB against the electric-heater card.

social.video_title: He called a propane tank a patio heater — Part 1/2
social.description: Upstairs at 10:41, a hiss, and an electric-heater card. I sent the clip. Would you have closed the window?

parts.text: Paz called it a surge until the office matched the serial to a tank he was not permitted to run after ten. I printed the ticket, the card, and a still. The truck went to a plug-in lamp. Paz told the aisle the card was always about optics. Optics is a word vendors use when a collar is on video. Pad policy now has a second line: BTUS ARE NOT A HEATER AFTER TEN. I sleep. Paz unplugs. The alley finally sounds like footsteps.

social.video_title: BTUs are not a heater after ten — Part 2/2
social.description: After-ten ticket, a plug-in lamp, and a second line on the card. Was a surge ever a tank?
